podcast.body: A cover of a 1967 rocksteady song by Jamaican vocal group The Paragons, "The Tide Is High" was released in the fall of 1980. Debbie Harry discovered the song from a compilation tape during a late 70s visit to London and initially wanted to record it with British ska band The Specials. After The Specials declined, Blondie recorded it themselves for their *Autoamerican* album. It took twelve weeks to reach number one on the Hot 100, affirming Blondie's "could do no wrong" status and becoming their third number one hit in different genres (disco, electro rock, reggae). "The Tide Is High is arguably the record that affirmed Blondie's imperial could do no wrong status."

podcast.body: Blondie's cover of John Holt's 1967 song, released on their 1980 album "Autoamerican," achieved widespread success, hitting number one in January 1981 and demonstrating the band's innovative engagement with the reggae genre on its own terms. "Blondie's number one cover of The Tie His High. The tie is high, but I'm holding on."
